//: M7 (SIG MCX-SPEAR), the U.S. Army's NGSW rifle in 6.8x51 Common Cartridge, 13-inch barrel, select-fire. Replaces the M4 in close-combat formations.
description: The M7, the U.S. Army's Next Generation Squad Weapon rifle, a SIG MCX-SPEAR chambered for the high-pressure 6.8x51mm Common Cartridge.  It hits harder and punches through body armor that would shrug off 5.56, at the cost of weight and recoil.  Feeds from 20- or 25-round SPEAR magazines.

//: M8, the short-barreled carbine variant of the M7 SPEAR in 6.8x51, ~11.5-inch barrel for CQB and vehicle crews. Louder and a touch less reach than the M7, far handier.
description: The M8, a short-barreled carbine cut down from the M7 SPEAR for close quarters and vehicle crews.  The stubby 6.8x51 barrel trades a little velocity and a lot of muzzle blast for a weapon that swings fast inside a building.  Feeds from SPEAR magazines.

//: M250 (XM250), the U.S. Army's NGSW automatic rifle/LMG in 6.8x51 Common Cartridge, belt-fed, replacing the M249 SAW in the squad. Heavier-hitting, armor-defeating support fire.
description: The M250, the belt-fed half of the Next Generation Squad Weapon program, a light machine gun in 6.8x51mm Common Cartridge.  It gives a squad's automatic rifleman the reach and armor penetration of a 7.62 gun in a package not much heavier than the 5.56 SAW it replaces.  Feeds from disintegrating belts.
